device.description: 10-bit quad voltage-output DAC with I2C interface and power-down
device.note: dac6574.pdf (SLAS408) p.2 pinout (DGS, pin descriptions; VDD is also the reference), p.3 electrical characteristics (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, logic levels vs VDD), p.4-5 I2C timing, p.13 update sequence, address and broadcast address bytes, p.14 control byte (Table 1, C7 C6 = 0 0), p.15 Table 2 control byte modes, MSB/LSB bytes and default read-back, p.16 registers (Table 3), p.18-19 write sequences (Tables 4-5), p.21-22 read-back (Tables 6-7), p.22 power-on reset to zero, p.23 Table 8 power-down modes

pages: p.2 (pinout), p.3 (VDD, logic levels), p.4-5 (I2C timing), p.13-16 (address, control byte, Table 2, registers), p.18-22 (write/read sequences), p.22-23 (power-on reset, power-down)
notModeled: analog outputs, reference and power-down output loads (power-down bits stored in the internal PDN register only; outputs never driven)

multi-word transactions: the datasheet lets MSB/LSB byte pairs repeat after one control byte until STOP / repeated START (Table 4 note 2); the model decodes only the last control byte + MSB + LSB (or the lone control byte) before the transaction ends (align end)
power-down bits are kept per channel in PDN and take effect immediately: the TRx-only (L=00) and DACx (L=01) distinction for power-down data is not modeled; normal data writes do not clear them
broadcast I2C address 1001 0000 (responds regardless of the address pins) is not expressible; the broadcast-mode control bytes (L=11) are decoded at the device's own address
C7 C6 must be 0 0 (bytes with them set are ignored, except broadcast mode which treats them as don't care)
read-back returns the temporary register of the selected channel (the datasheet does not say whether TRx or DRx is read)
address pins latched at power-up (the model reads them live)
I2C high-speed mode master code and timing
variants: DAC6574 has its own datasheet; DAC5574 / DAC7574 (8/12-bit) are the same family with other data widths
